solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gladys Oates excitedly cuddling senior chap in the third row

indicators.note: the shuffled name wraps its arms round the next piece, holding it inside
worked up, these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a senior person is older, so old

explanation.surface: A woman called Gladys Oates gets giddy hugging an elderly man sitting three rows back.
explanation.walkthrough: The third row of the grid reads ANCIENT MARINER (9 and 10 across), so the definition points at that pair of entries rather than at a seat in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ancient Mariner, the figure in row three of the grid, is a weathered veteran sailor, a fellow of exactly this kind.

clue.text: Young ladies upset about the introduction of nasty, common language

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the next letter
in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: gals is a casual word for young women

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Girls get cross when someone starts using rude, vulgar words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses GALS to SLAG, and 'about' puts N, from 'the introduction of nasty', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, everyday vocabulary, the common talk of ordinary speakers rather than standard usage.

clue.text: You can set your watch by this diet period

definitions.text: You can set your watch by this

parts.note: lo-cal, short for low-calorie, describes a diet
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone claims their eating regime is so regular you could time a clock by it.
explanation.walkthrough: LO-CAL is the advertising contraction of 'low calorie', a diet food label.
explanation.definitionFit: When travelling you reset a wristwatch to the hour kept in the place you have arrived at.

clue.text: Bond's return, strangely idle following the completion of Octopussy

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the picked letter
the completion of a word is its final letter
strangely says the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sounds like James Bond coming back, oddly lazy, after finishing the film Octopussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' is a financial bond, not 007, and Octopussy is only there to end in the right letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The yield of a bond is the income or return it pays its holder, expressed as a percentage.

clue.text: Most recent Latin advanced paper

parts.note: A is short for advanced, as in A level
an exam paper is a test

explanation.surface: The newest thing is an advanced Latin exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Latest means newest, the most up-to-date of a series.

clue.text: Aggregate taken from Hilversum to Tallinn

indicators.note: the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A total of distance or cost covered on a trip from a Dutch town to the Estonian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is the whole amount when everything is added together.

clue.text: Displays three-wheeler, shot from above

parts.note: to air something is to display it, so airs means displays
a trike is a tricycle, a three-wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a three-wheeled bike, photographed from overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: An air strike is an attack made by aircraft, firing or bombing on targets below.

clue.text: Proprietor's wife stuck in revolting Nevada resort

definitions.note: read as 'Proprietor is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the letter is lodged inside the resort's name
revolting means turning over, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Reno is a gambling resort city in Nevada

explanation.surface: A business owner's wife is trapped in a disgusting Nevada holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts W into RENO giving RWENO, and 'revolting' turns that round. The definition is 'Proprietor' with 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who possesses a business or property.

clue.text: Firm discipline used to press crew member

parts.note: an iron is used to press clothes
a hand is a member of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: Strict rules are used to press-gang someone into a ship's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling with an iron hand means governing with strict, unyielding control.

clue.text: Regularly taking out nanny? Crikey, not very old!

indicators.note: every other letter is removed, leaving a regular selection of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone surprised that a nanny is not very old after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' here is fodder, not a negation of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means extremely aged, belonging to the distant past.

clue.text: Colliery worker defending Arab collier?

indicators.note: the worker wraps round and protects the abbreviation

parts.note: a miner works in a colliery, a coal mine
Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A coal miner sticks up for a man from Arabia who also works with coal.
explanation.walkthrough: A collier is also a coal-carrying ship, or a sailor on one; the question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier can be a seaman on a coal ship, so a seafaring man by trade.

clue.text: Frosty starts to General Election leaders' interactive debates

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The opening of televised election debates between party leaders is chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid means icy cold, a literary word for freezing or frosty.

clue.text: Having made the cut, rookie enters golf club

indicators.note: the beginner goes into the middle of the cut word

parts.note: shorn means cut, as of hair or a fleece
a tiro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: A newcomer survives the halfway cut and joins a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made the cut' sounds like golf but means shorn.
explanation.definitionFit: A short iron is one of the higher-numbered irons, used for short approach shots in golf.

clue.text: 10 shillings, first class? Good Lord!

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money
A1 means first class, with the digit read as the letter I
lor is a dialect form of Lord used as an exclamation

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished at a ten-shilling first-class fare.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is not money: it points to 10 across, MARINER. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, so the same as a sailor.

clue.text: Model shod in sensible footwear

indicators.note: the reshaped letters go inside the word for sensible

parts.note: sane means sensible, of sound mind

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the word is remoulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion model wears practical shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' rearranges SHOD to DSHO, which goes into SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandshoe is a canvas plimsoll, a type of light shoe for the beach.

clue.text: Oleaginous products 13 across's girlfriend owns, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that sounds like the one entered

parts.note: Popeye the Sailor's girlfriend is Olive Oyl, and the 's means things she owns

explanation.surface: The girlfriend of a seaman owns some greasy merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is SAILOR: Popeye the Sailor's girlfriend in the cartoons is Olive Oyl.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed from fruit, these are fatty liquid goods, so oily in nature.

clue.text: Boatman adrift round island region bordering Hudson Bay

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the single letter
adrift means loose and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boatman drifting around an island in Canada's northern bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is a Canadian province whose north-east coast lies on Hudson Bay.

clue.text: Large area cordoned by random shotgun attack

indicators.note: the two letters are fenced in by the shuffled word
random says the letters come in no fixed order

explanation.surface: Police cordon off a big zone after an indiscriminate shotgun attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' rearranges SHOTGUN to ONSUGHT, and 'cordoned by' puts LA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, sweeping assault.

clue.text: He's paid to kill Jenny with arsenic (a serious offence)

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, an ass
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
a sin is a grave wrong

explanation.surface: A hired killer poisons a woman named Jenny with arsenic, a grave crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like a victim's name but is a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired killer, typically of a prominent figure.

clue.text: Shawnee dies trying to protect those most desperate

indicators.note: the outer words protect the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A Native American warrior falls defending the weakest of the tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediest describes people in the greatest want, used here as a noun for the poorest.

clue.text: Stopped to relax in the outskirts of Chelmsford

indicators.note: the word for relax sits inside the two letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to ease is to relax or loosen

explanation.surface: Someone pulled over to unwind on the edge of an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelmsford is the county town of Essex; its outskirts give C and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased means came to an end or halted.

clue.text: Arenas to remain expensive, according to reports

indicators.note: reports are spoken accounts, so the words are rendered by their sound

parts.note: to stay is to remain and dear means expensive

explanation.surface: Sports venues will keep their prices high, the press say.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, a sports ground with tiers of seating.

clue.text: U-boat officer losing place he is renting from another leaseholder

definitions.text: he is renting from another leaseholder

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub

indicators.note: losing says the officer loses the word for place

parts.note: a lieutenant is a military officer
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: A submarine officer is evicted and must rent from someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtenant leases from a tenant rather than directly from the property's owner.

clue.text: Bishop took food infused with hot dip

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the meal word has the letter steeped into it

parts.note: ate means took food
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A bishop ate something spicy with a hot sauce for dipping.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip is to take a quick swim, which is what bathing means.

clue.text: See 27
House Bertie's Little pal?

definitions.meaning: house is another name for the numbers game of calling and marking cards
Bertie Wooster's friend in P. G. Wodehouse is the hapless ... Little

explanation.surface: Asking whether a home belongs to a small friend of someone named Bertie.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital L on 'Little' hides a surname. House is the British name for the same game, called when a card is full.
explanation.definitionFit: House is the game's alternative name; Bingo Little is Bertie Wooster's friend in Wodehouse.

clue.text: Look into hospital, where cuts are commonplace

indicators.note: the word for look goes inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: An inspection of a hospital where budget cuts are routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' looks like spending cuts or surgery; it means haircuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair salon is a place where people routinely have their hair trimmed.

clue.text: Is too smart for old, upper-class Charlies

parts.note: U denotes upper-class in British usage
a charlie is a fool, so twits

explanation.surface: A clever person runs rings round some posh old fools.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'charlie' is British slang for a fool, a twit.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart someone is to beat them by cleverness.

clue.text: Accomplished objective, taking over county

parts.note: done means accomplished, finished

indicators.note: taking away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a goal is an objective
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Having achieved an aim, someone takes control of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking over' is not seizing control: it removes O (cricket's abbreviation for an over) from GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Playing around, sneakily obtains crafty pleasures

parts.note: messing about means fooling or playing around

indicators.note: sneakily suggests the letters slip into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone fooling around craftily gets what they enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' refers to craft, boats. 'sneakily' rearranges OBTAINS. The phrase is Ratty's in The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft are vessels, so the delights of boating are pleasures involving craft.
